text: Zina made haste to bring this, to her, painful scene to an end.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She stretched her pretty hand silently to the prince, and even forced herself to smile.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: The prince reverently took the little hand into his own, and covered it with kisses.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I am only this mo—ment beginning to live,” he mutterred, in a voice that seemed choking with rapture and ecstasy.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Zina,” began Maria Alexandrovna, solemnly, “look well at this man! This is the most honest and upright and noble man of all the men I know. He is a knight of the middle ages! But she knows it, Prince, she knows it too well; to my grief I say it. Oh! why did you come here? I am surrendering my treasure to you—my angel! Oh! take care of her, Prince. Her mother entreats you to watch over her. And what mother could blame my grief!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Enough, mamma! that’s enough,” said Zina, quietly.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Protect her from all hurt and insult, Prince! Can I rely upon your sword to flash in the face of the vile scandal-monger who dares to offend my Zina?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Enough, mother, I tell you! am I——?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes, ye—yes, it shall flash all right,” said the prince.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But I want to be married now, at once. I—I’m only just learning what it is to live. I want to send off to Donchanovo at once. I want to send for some di—iamonds I have there. I want to lay them at her feet.——I——”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What noble ardour! what ecstasy of love! what noble, generous feelings you have, Prince!” cried Maria Alexandrovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “And you could bury yourself—bury yourself, far from the world and society! I shall remind you of this a thousand times! I go mad when I think of that hellish woman.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What could I do? I was fri—ghtened!” stammered the prince in a whining voice: “they wanted to put me in a lu—unatic asylum! I was dreadfully alarmed!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “In a lunatic asylum? Ah, the scoundrels! oh, the inhuman wretches! Ah, the low cunning of them! Yes, Prince; I had heard of it. But the lunacy was in these people, not in you. Why, why was it—what for?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I don’t know myself, what it was for,” replied the poor old man, feebly sinking into his chair; “I was at a ball, don’t you know, and told some an—ecdote or other and they didn’t like it; and so they got up a scandal and a ro—ow.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Surely that was not all, Prince?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “No;—the—I was playing cards with Prince Paul De—mentieff, and I was cleared out: you see, I had two kings and three quee—ns, three kings and two qu—eens; or I should say—one king—and some queens—I know I had——.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “And it was for this? Oh, the hellish inhumanity of some people! You are weeping, Prince; but be of good cheer—it is all over now! Now I shall be at hand, dearest Prince,—I shall not leave Zina; and we shall see which of them will dare to say a word to you, then! And do you know, my Prince, your marriage will expose them! it will shame them! They will see that you are a man—that a lovely girl like our Zina would never have married a madman! You shall raise your head proudly now, and look them straight in the face!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes; I shall look them straight in the f—ace!” murmured the prince, slowly shutting his eyes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna saw that her work was done: the prince was tired out with love and emotion.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She was only wasting her eloquence!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Prince, you are disturbed and tired, I see you are!” she said; “you must rest, you must take a good rest after so much agitation,” she added, bending over him maternally.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes, ye—yes; I should like to lie down a little,” said the old man.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Of course, of course! you must lie down! those agitating scenes——stop, I will escort you myself, and arrange your couch with my own hands! Why are you looking so hard at that portrait, Prince? That is my mother’s picture; she was an angel—not a woman! Oh, why is she not among us at this joyful moment!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes; charming—charming!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Do you know, I had a mother too,—a princess, and imagine! a re—markably, a re—markably fat woman she was; but that is not what I was going to say,——I—I feel a little weak, and——Au revoir, my charming child—to-morrow—to-day—I will—I—I—Au revoir, au revoir!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Here the poor old fellow tried to kiss his hand, but slipped, and nearly fell over the threshold of the door.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Take care, dear Prince—take care! lean on my arm!” cried Maria Alexandrovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Charming, ch—arming!” he muttered, as he left the room.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I am only now le—learning to live!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Zina was left alone.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: A terrible oppression weighed down her heart.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She felt a sensation of loathing which nearly suffocated her.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She despised herself—her cheeks burned.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: With folded hands, and teeth biting hard into her lips, she stood in one spot, motionless.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: The tears of shame streamed from her eyes,——and at this moment the door opened, and Paul Mosgliakoff entered the room!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: He had heard all—all.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: He did not actually enter the room, but stood at the door, pale with excitement and fury.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Zina looked at him in amazement.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “So that’s the sort of person you are!” he cried panting.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “At last I have found you out, have I?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Found me out?” repeated Zina, looking at him as though he were a madman.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Suddenly her eyes flashed with rage.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “How dare you address me like that?” she cried, advancing towards him.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I have heard all!” said Mosgliakoff solemnly, but involuntarily taking a step backwards.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “You heard? I see—you have been eavesdropping!” cried Zina, looking at him with disdain.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, I have been eavesdropping! Yes—I consented to do a mean action, and my reward is that I have found out that you, too, are——I don’t know how to express to you what I think you!” he replied, looking more and more timid under Zina’s eyes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “And supposing that you have heard all: what right have you to blame me? What right have you to speak to me so insolently, in any case?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I!—I? what right have I? and you can ask me this? You are going to marry this prince, and I have no right to say a word! Why, you gave me your promise—is that nothing?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “When?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “How, when?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Did not I tell you that morning, when you came to me with your sentimental nonsense—did I not tell you that I could give you no decided answer?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But you did not reject me; you did not send me away. I see—you kept me hanging in reserve, in case of need! You lured me into your net! I see, I see it all!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: An expression of pain flitted over Zina’s careworn face, as though someone had suddenly stabbed her to the heart; but she mastered her feelings.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “If I didn’t turn you out of the house,” she began deliberately and very clearly, though her voice had a scarcely perceptible tremor in it, “I refrained from such a course purely out of pity. You begged me yourself to postpone, to give you time, not to say you ‘No,’ to study you better, and ‘then,’ you said, ‘then, when you know what a fine fellow I am, perhaps you will not refuse me! These were your own words, or very like them, at the very beginning of your courtship!—you cannot deny them! And now you dare to tell me that I ‘lured you into my net,’ just as though you did not notice my expression of loathing when you made your appearance this morning! You came a fortnight sooner than I expected you, and I did not hide my disgust; on the contrary, I made it evident—you must have noticed it—I know you did; because you asked me whether I was angry because you had come sooner than you promised! Let me tell you that people who do not, and do not care to, hide their loathing for a man can hardly be accused of luring that man into their net! You dare to tell me that I was keeping you in reserve! Very well; my answer to that is, that I judged of you like this: ‘Though he may not be endowed with much intellect, still he may turn out to be a good enough fellow; and if so, it might be possible to marry him. However, being persuaded, now, that you are a fool, and a mischievous fool into the bargain,—having found out this fact, to my great joy,—it only remains for me now to wish you every happiness and a pleasant journey. Good-bye!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: With these words Zina turned her back on him, and deliberately made for the door.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff, seeing that all was lost, boiled over with fury.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh! so I’m a fool!” he yelled; “I’m a fool, am I? Very well, good-bye! But before I go, the whole town shall know of this! They shall all hear how you and your mother made the old man drunk, and then swindled him! I shall let the whole world know it! You shall see what Mosgliakoff can do!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Zina trembled and stopped, as though to answer; but on reflection, she contented herself by shrugging her shoulders; glanced contemptuously at Mosgliakoff, and left the room, banging the door after her.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: At this moment Maria Alexandrovna made her appearance.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She heard Mosgliakoff’s exclamation, and, divining at once what had happened, trembled with terror.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff still in the house, and near the prince!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff about to spread the news all over the town!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: At this moment, when secrecy, if only for a short time, was essential!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: But Maria Alexandrovna was quick at calculations: she thought, with an eagle flight of the mind, over all the circumstances of the case, and her plan for the pacification of Mosgliakoff was ready in an instant!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What is it, mon ami?” she said, entering the room, and holding out her hand to him with friendly warmth.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “How—‘mon ami?’ ” cried the enraged Mosgliakoff.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Mon ami, indeed! the moment after you have abused and reviled me like a pickpocket! No, no! Not quite so green, my good lady! I’m not to be so easily imposed upon again!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I am sorry, extremely sorry, to see you in such a strange condition of mind, Paul Alexandrovitch! What expressions you use! You do not take the trouble to choose your words before ladies—oh, fie!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Before ladies? Ho ho! You—you are—you are anything you like—but not a lady!” yelled Mosgliakoff.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I don’t quite know what he meant, but it was something very terrible, you may be sure!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna looked benignly in his face:

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Sit down!” she said, sorrowfully, showing him a chair, the same that the old prince had reclined in a quarter of an hour before.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But listen, will you listen, Maria Alexandrovna? You look at me just as though you were not the least to blame; in fact, as though I were the guilty party! Really, Maria Alexandrovna, this is a little too much of a good thing! No human being can stand that sort of thing, Maria Alexandrovna! You must be aware of that fact!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “My dear friend,” replied Maria Alexandrovna—“you will allow me to continue to call you by that name, for you have no better friend than I am!—my friend, you are suffering—you are amazed and bewildered; your heart is sore, and therefore the tone of your remarks to me is perhaps not surprising. But I have made up my mind to open my heart to you, especially as I am, perhaps, in some degree to blame before you. Sit down; let us talk it over!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna’s voice was tender to a sickly extent.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Her face showed the pain she was suffering.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: The amazed Mosgliakoff sat down beside her in the arm-chair.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “You hid somewhere, and listened, I suppose?” she began, looking reproachfully into his face.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes I did, of course I did; and a good thing too! What a fool I should have looked if I hadn’t! At all events now I know what you have been plotting against me!” replied the injured man, rudely; encouraging and supporting himself by his own fury.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “And you—and you—with your principles, and with your bringing up, could condescend to such an action—Oh, oh!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff jumped up.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Maria Alexandrovna, this is a little too much!” he cried.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Consider what you condescend to do, with your principles, and then judge of other people.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “One more question,” she continued, without replying to his outburst: “who recommended you to be an eavesdropper; who told you anything; who is the spy here? That’s what I wish to know!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, excuse me; that I shall not tell you!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Very well; I know already. I said, Paul, that I was in some degree to blame before you. But if you look into the matter you will find that if I am to blame it is solely in consequence of my anxiety to do you a good turn!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What? a good turn—me? No, no, madam! I assure you I am not to be caught again! I’m not quite such a fool!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: He moved so violently in his arm-chair that it shook again.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Now, do be cool, if you can, my good friend.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Listen to me attentively, and you will find that what I say is only the bare truth.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: In the first place I was anxious to inform you of all that has just taken place, in which case you would have learned everything, down to the smallest detail, without being obliged to descend to eavesdropping!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: If I did not tell you all before, it was simply because the whole matter was in an embryo condition in my mind.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: It was then quite possible that what has happened would never happen.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: You see, I am quite open with you.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “In the second place, do not blame my daughter. She loves you to distraction; and it was only by the exercise of my utmost influence that I persuaded her to drop you, and accept the prince’s offer.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I have just had the pleasure of receiving convincing proof of her ‘love to distraction!’ ” remarked Mosgliakoff, ironically and bitterly.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Very well. But how did you speak to her? As a lover should speak? Again, ought any man of respectable position and tone to speak like that? You insulted and wounded her!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Never mind about my ‘tone’ now! All I can say is that this morning, when I went away with the prince, in spite of both of you having been as sweet as honey to me before, you reviled me behind my back like a pickpocket! I know all about it, you see!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, from the same dirty source, I suppose?” said Maria Alexandrovna, smiling disdainfully.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, Paul, I did revile you: I pitched into you considerably, and I admit it frankly. But it was simply that I was bound to blacken you before her. Why? Because, as I have said, I required her to consent to leave you, and this consent was so difficult to tear from her! Short-sighted man that you are! If she had not loved you, why should I have required so to blacken your character? Why should I have been obliged to take this extreme step? Oh! you don’t know all! I was forced to use my fullest maternal authority in order to erase you from her heart; and with all my influence and skill I only succeeded in erasing your dear image superficially and partially! If you saw and heard all just now, it cannot have escaped you that Zina did not once, by either word or gesture, encourage or confirm my words to the prince? Throughout the whole scene she said not one word. She sang, but like an automaton! Her whole soul was in anguish, and at last, out of pity for her, I took the prince away. I am sure, she cried, when I left her alone! When you entered the room you must have observed tears in her eyes?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff certainly did recall the fact that when he rushed into the room Zina was crying.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But you—you—why were you so against me, Maria Alexandrovna?” he cried.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Why did you revile me and malign me, as you admit you did?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ah, now that’s quite a different question. Now, if you had only asked me reasonably at the beginning, you should have had your answer long ago! Yes, you are right. It was I, and I alone, who did it all. Do not think of Zina in the matter. Now, why did I do it? I reply, in the first place, for Zina’s sake. The prince is rich, influential, has great connections, and in marrying him Zina will make a brilliant match. Very well; then if the prince dies—as perhaps he will die soon, for we are all mortal,—Zina is still young, a widow, a princess, and probably very rich. Then she can marry whom she pleases; she may make another brilliant match if she likes. But of course she will marry the man she loves, and loved before, the man whose heart she wounded by accepting the prince. Remorse alone would be enough to make her marry the man whom she had loved and so deeply injured!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Hem!” said Paul, gazing at his boots thoughtfully.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “In the second place,” continued Maria, “and I will put this shortly, because, though you read a great deal of your beloved Shakespeare, and extract his finest thoughts and ideals, yet you are very young, and cannot, perhaps, apply what you read.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: You may not understand my feelings in this matter: listen, however.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I am giving my Zina to this prince partly for the prince’s own sake, because I wish to save him by this marriage.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: We are old friends; he is the dearest and best of men, he is a knightly, chivalrous gentleman, and he lives helpless and miserable in the claws of that devil of a woman at Donchanovo!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Heaven knows that I persuaded Zina into this marriage by putting it to her that she would be performing a great and noble action.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I represented her as being the stay and the comfort and the darling and the idol of a poor old man, who probably would not live another year at the most!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I showed her that thus his last days should be made happy with love and light and friendship, instead of wretched with fear and the society of a detestable woman.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Oh! do not blame Zina.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She is guiltless.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I am not—I admit it; for if there have been calculations it is I who have made them!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: But I calculated for her, Paul; for her, not myself!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I have outlived my time; I have thought but for my child, and what mother could blame me for this?

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Tears sparkled in the fond mother’s eyes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff listened in amazement to all this eloquence, winking his eyes in bewilderment.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, yes, of course! You talk well, Maria Alexandrovna, but you forget—you gave me your word, you encouraged me, you gave me my hopes; and where am I now? I have to stand aside and look a fool!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But, my dear Paul, you don’t surely suppose that I have not thought of you too! Don’t you see the huge, immeasurable gain to yourself in all this? A gain so vast that I was bound in your interest to act as I did!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Gain for me! How so?” asked Paul, in the most abject state of confusion and bewilderment.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Gracious Heavens! do you mean to say you are really so simple and so short-sighted as to be unable to see that?” cried Maria Alexandrovna, raising her eyes to the ceiling in a pious manner.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh! youth, youth! That’s what comes of steeping one’s soul in Shakespeare! You ask me, my dear friend Paul, where is the gain to you in all this. Allow me to make a little digression. Zina loves you—that is an undoubted fact. But I have observed that at the same time, and in spite of her evident love, she is not quite sure of your good feeling and devotion to her; and for this reason she is sometimes cold and self-restrained in your presence. Have you never observed this yourself, Paul?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Certainly; I did this very day; but go on, what do you deduce from that fact?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “There, you see! you have observed it yourself; then of course I am right. She is not quite sure of the lasting quality of your feeling for her! I am a mother, and I may be permitted to read the heart of my child. Now, then, supposing that instead of rushing into the room and reproaching, vilifying, even swearing at and insulting this sweet, pure, beautiful, proud being, instead of hurling contempt and vituperation at her head—supposing that instead of all this you had received the bad news with composure, with tears of grief, maybe; perhaps even with despair—but at the same time with noble composure of soul——”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “No, no—don’t interrupt me! I wish to show you the picture as it is. Very well, supposing, then, that you had come to her and said, ‘Zina, I love you better than my life, but family considerations must separate us; I understand these considerations—they are devised for your greater happiness, and I dare not oppose them. Zina, I forgive you; be happy, if you can!’—think what effect such noble words would have wrought upon her heart!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes—yes, that’s all very true, I quite understand that much! but if I had said all this, I should have had to go all the same, without satisfaction!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “No, no, no! don’t interrupt me!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I wish to show you the whole picture in all its detail, in order to impress you fully and satisfactorily.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Very well, then, imagine now that you meet her in society some time afterwards: you meet perhaps at a ball—in the brilliant light of a ball-room, under the soothing strains of music, and in the midst of worldly women and of all that is gay and beautiful.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: You alone are sad—thoughtful—pale,—you lean against some pillar (where you are visible, however!) and watch her.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She is dancing.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: You hear the strains of Strauss, and the wit and merriment around you, but you are sad and wretched.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What, think you, will Zina make of it? With what sort of eyes will she gaze on you as you stand there? ‘And I could doubt this man!’ she will think, ‘this man who sacrificed all, all, for my sake—even to the mortal wounding of his heart! Of course the old love will awake in her bosom and will swell with irresistible power!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna stopped to take breath.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Paul moved violently from side to side of his chair.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Zina now goes abroad for the benefit of the prince’s health—to Italy—to Spain,” she continued, “where the myrtle and the lemon tree grow, where the sky is so blue, the beautiful Guadalquiver flows! to the land of love, where none can live without loving; where roses and kisses—so to speak—breathe in the very air around. You follow her—you sacrifice your business, friends, everything, and follow her. And so your love grows and increases with irresistible might. Of course that love is irreproachable—innocent—you will languish for one another—you will meet frequently; of course others will malign and vilify you both, and call your love by baser names—but your love is innocent, as I have purposely said; I am her mother—it is not for me to teach you evil, but good. At all events the prince is not in the condition to keep a very sharp look-out upon you; but if he did, as if there would be the slightest ground for base suspicion? Well, the prince dies at last, and then, who will marry Zina, if not yourself? You are so distant a relative of the prince’s that there could be no obstacle to the match; you marry her—she is young still, and rich. You are a grandee in an instant! you, too, are rich now! I will take care that the prince’s will is made as it should be; and lastly, Zina, now convinced of your loyalty and faithfulness, will look on you hereafter as her hero, as her paragon of virtue and self-sacrifice! Oh! you must be blind,—blind, not to observe and calculate your own profit when it lies but a couple of strides from you, grinning at you, as it were, and saying, ‘Here, I am yours, take me! text: “Oh, dear prince, do marry!” chirped another.

text: “Marry, marry, do marry!” was now the cry on all sides.

text: “Ye—yes. Why should I not ma—arry!” said the old man, confused and bewildered with all the cries and exclamations around him.

text: “Ye—yes, my boy, quite so; I un—derstand what you mean. I may as well tell you, ladies, that I am not in a position to marry again; and having passed one most delightful evening with our fascinating hostess, I must start away to-morrow to the Hermitage, and then I shall go straight off abroad, and study the question of the enlightenment of Europe.”

text: But Maria Alexandrovna had now made up her mind how to act; all this while she had played a mere waiting game, observing closely and carefully all that was said or done, although she could see only too clearly that her plans were undermined, and that her foes had come about her in numbers which were too great to be altogether pleasant.

text: At last, however, she comprehended the situation, she thought, completely.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She had gauged how the matter stood in all its branches, and she determined to slay the hundred-headed hydra at one fell blow!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: With great majesty, then, she rose from her seat, and approached the tea-table, stalking across the room with firm and dignified tread, as she looked around upon her pigmy foes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: The fire of inspiration blazed in her eyes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She resolved to smite once, and annihilate this vile nest of poisonous scandal-adders: to destroy the miserable Mosgliakoff, as though he were a blackbeetle, and with one triumphant blow to reassert all her influence over this miserable old idiot-prince!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Some audacity was requisite for such a performance, of course; but Maria Alexandrovna had not even to put her hand in her pocket for a supply of that particular commodity.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Mesdames,” she began, solemnly, and with much dignity (Maria Alexandrovna was always a great admirer of solemnity); “mesdames, I have been a listener to your conversation—to your witty remarks and merry jokes—long enough, and I consider that my turn has come, at last, to put in a word in contribution.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “You are aware we have all met here accidentally (to my great joy, I must add—to my very great joy); but, though I should be the first to refuse to divulge a family secret before the strictest rules of ordinary propriety rendered such a revelation necessary, yet, as my dear guest here appears to me to have given us to understand, by covert hints and insinuations, that he is not averse to the matter becoming common property (he will forgive me if I have mistaken his intentions!)—I cannot help feeling that the prince is not only not averse, but actually desires me to make known our great family secret. Am I right, Prince?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes, quite so, quite so! Very glad, ve—ry glad, I’m sure!” said the prince, who had not the remotest idea what the good lady was talking about!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna, for greater effect, now paused to take breath, and looked solemnly and proudly around upon the assembled guests, all of whom were now listening with greedy but slightly disturbed curiosity to what their hostess was about to reveal to them.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff shuddered; Zina flushed up, and arose from her seat; Afanassy, seeing that something important was about to happen, blew his nose violently, in order to be ready for any emergency.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, ladies; I am ready—nay, gratified—to entrust my family secret to your keeping!——This evening, the prince, overcome by the beauty and virtues of my daughter, has done her the honour of proposing to me for her hand. Prince,” she concluded, in trembling tearful accents, “dear Prince; you must not, you cannot blame me for my candour! It is only my overwhelming joy that could have torn this dear secret prematurely from my heart: and what mother is there who will blame me in such a case as this?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Words fail me to describe the effect produced by this most unexpected sally on the part of Maria Alexandrovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: All present appeared to be struck dumb with amazement.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: These perfidious guests, who had thought to frighten Maria Alexandrovna by showing her that they knew her secret; who thought to annihilate her by the premature revelation of that secret; who thought to overwhelm her, for the present, with their hints and insinuations; these guests were themselves struck down and pulverized by this fearless candour on her part!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Such audacious frankness argued the consciousness of strength.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “So that the prince actually, and of his own free-will is really going to marry Zina? So they did not drink and bully and swindle him into it? So he is not to be married burglariously and forcibly? So Maria Alexandrovna is not afraid of anybody? Then we can’t knock this marriage on the head—since the prince is not being married compulsorily!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Such were the questions and exclamations the visitors now put to themselves and each other.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: But very soon the whispers which the hostess’s words had awakened all over the room, suddenly changed to chirps and exclamations of joy.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Natalia Dimitrievna was the first to come forward and embrace Maria Alexandrovna; then came Mrs. Antipova; next Felisata Michaelovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: All present were shortly on their feet and moving about, changing places.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Many of the ladies were pale with rage.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Some began to congratulate Zina, who was confused enough without; some attached themselves to the wretched Afanassy Matveyevitch.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna stretched her arms theatrically, and embraced her daughter—almost by force.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: The prince alone gazed upon the company with a sort of confused wonder; but he smiled on as before.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: He seemed to be pleased with the scene.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: At sight of the mother and daughter embracing, he took out his handkerchief, and wiped his eye, in the corner of which there really was a tear.

text: Of course the company fell upon him with their congratulations before very long.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I congratulate you, Prince! I congratulate you!” came from all sides at once.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “So you are going to be married, Prince?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “So you really are going to marry?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Dear Prince! You really are to be married, then?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes, ye—yes; quite so, quite so!” replied the old fellow, delighted beyond measure with all the rapture and atmosphere of congratulation around him; “and I confess what I like best of all, is the ve—ery kind in—terest you all take in me! I shall never forget it, never for—get it! Charming! charming! You have brought the tears to my eyes!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Kiss me, prince!” cried Felisata Michaelovna, in stentorian tones.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “And I con—fess further,” continued the Prince, as well as the constant physical interruptions from all sides allowed him; “I confess I am beyond measure as—tonished that Maria Alexandrovna, our revered hostess, should have had the extraordinary penet—ration to guess my dream! She might have dreamed it herself, instead of me. Ex—traordinary perspicacity! Won—derful, wonderful!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, prince; your dream again!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, come, prince! admit—confess!” cried one and all.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, prince, it is no use concealing it now; it is time we divulged this secret of ours!” said Maria Alexandrovna, severely and decidedly.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I quite entered into your refined, allegorical manner; the delightful delicacy with which you gave me to understand, by means of subtle insinuations, that you wished the fact of your engagement to be made known. Yes, ladies, it is all true! This very evening the prince knelt at my daughter’s feet, and actually, and by no means in a dream, made a solemn proposal of marriage to her!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes—yes, quite so! just exactly like that; and under the very cir—cumstances she describes: just like re—ality,” said the old man.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “My dear young lady,” he continued, bowing with his greatest courtesy to Zina, who had by no means recovered from her amazement as yet; “my dear young lady, I swear to you, I should never have dared thus to bring your name into pro—minence, if others had not done so before me! It was a most be—witching dream! a be—witching dream! and I am doubly happy that I have been per—mitted to describe it. Charming—charming!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Dear me! how very curious it is: he insists on sticking to his idea about a dream!” whispered Mrs. Antipova to the now slightly paling Maria Alexandrovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Alas! that great woman had felt her heart beating more quickly than she liked without this last little reminder!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What does it mean?” whispered the ladies among themselves.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Excuse me, prince,” began Maria Alexandrovna, with a miserable attempt at a smile, “but I confess you astonish me a great deal! What is this strange idea of yours about a dream? I confess I had thought you were joking up to this moment; but—if it be a joke on your part, it is exceedingly out of place! I should like—I am anxious to ascribe your conduct to absence of mind, but——”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes; it may really be a case of absence of mind!” put in Natalia Dimitrievna in a whisper.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes—yes—of course, quite so; it may easily be absence of mind!” confirmed the prince, who clearly did not in the least comprehend what they were trying to get out of him; “and with regard to this subject, let me tell you a little an—ecdote. I was asked to a funeral at Petersburg, and I went and made a little mis—take about it and thought it was a birthday par—ty! So I brought a lovely bouquet of cam—ellias! When I came in and saw the master of the house lying in state on a table, I didn’t know where to lo—ok, or what to do with my ca—mellias, I assure you!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes; but, Prince, this is not the moment for stories!” observed Maria Alexandrovna, with great annoyance.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Of course, my daughter has no need to beat up a husband; but at the same time, I must repeat that you yourself here, just by the piano, made her an offer of marriage. I did not ask you to do it! I may say I was amazed to hear it! However, since the episode of your proposal, I may say that I have thought of nothing else; and I have only waited for your appearance to talk the matter over with you. But now—well, I am a mother, and this is my daughter. You speak of a dream. I supposed, naturally, that you were anxious to make your engagement known by the medium of an allegory. Well, I am perfectly well aware that someone may have thought fit to confuse your mind on this matter; in fact, I may say that I have my suspicions as to the individual responsible for such a——however, kindly explain yourself, Prince; explain yourself quickly and satisfactorily. You cannot be permitted to jest in this fashion in a respectable house.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes—quite so, quite so; one should not jest in respectable houses,” remarked the prince, still bewildered, but beginning gradually to grow a little disconcerted.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But that is no answer to my question, Prince. I ask you to reply categorically. I insist upon your confirming—confirming here and at once—the fact that this very evening you made a proposal of marriage to my daughter!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Quite so—quite so; I am ready to confirm that! But I have told the com—pany all about it, and Felisata Michaelovna ac—tually guessed my dream!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Not dream! it was not a dream!” shouted Maria Alexandrovna furiously.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “It was not a dream, Prince, but you were wide awake. Do you hear? Awake—you were awake!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Awake?” cried the prince, rising from his chair in astonishment.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Well, there you are, my friend; it has come about just as you said,” he added, turning to Mosgliakoff.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But I assure you, most es—teemed Maria Alexandrovna, that you are under a del—usion. I am quite convinced that I saw the whole scene in a dream!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Goodness gracious!” cried Maria Alexandrovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Do not disturb yourself, dear Maria Alexandrovna,” said Natalia Dimitrievna, “probably the prince has forgotten; he will recollect himself by and by.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I am astonished at you, Natalia Dimitrievna!” said the now furious hostess.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “As if people forget this sort of thing! Excuse me, Prince, but are you laughing at us, or what are you doing? Are you trying to act one of Dumas’ heroes, or Lauzun or Ferlacourt, or somebody? But, if you will excuse me saying so, you are a good deal too old for that sort of thing, and I assure you, your amiable little play-acting will not do here! My daughter is not a French viscountess! I tell you, this very evening and in this very spot here, my daughter sang a ballad to you, and you, amazed at the beauty of her singing, went down on your knees and made her a proposal of marriage. I am not talking in my sleep, am I? Surely I am wide awake? Speak, Prince, am I asleep, or not?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes, of course, of course—quite so. I don’t know,” said the bewildered old man.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I mean, I don’t think I am drea—ming now; but, a little while ago I was asleep, you see; and while asleep I had this dream, that I——”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Goodness me, Prince, I tell you you were not dreaming. Not dreaming, do you hear? Not dreaming! What on earth do you mean? Are you raving, Prince, or what?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes; deuce only knows. I don’t know! It seems to me I’m getting be—wildered,” said the prince, looking around him in a state of considerable mental perturbation.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But, my dear Prince, how can you possibly have dreamed this, when I can tell you all the minutest details of your proposal and of the circumstances attending it? You have not told any of us of these details. How could I possibly have known what you dreamed?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But, perhaps the prince did tell someone of his dream, in detail,” remarked Natalia Dimitrievna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes, quite so—quite so! Perhaps I did tell someone all about my dream, in detail,” said the now completely lost and bewildered prince.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Here’s a nice comedy!” whispered Felisata Michaelovna to her neighbour.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “My goodness me! this is too much for anybody’s patience!” cried Maria Alexandrovna, beside herself with helpless rage.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Do you hear me, Prince? She sang you a ballad—sang you a ballad! Surely you didn’t dream that too?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Certainly—cer—tainly, quite so. It really did seem to me that she sang me a ballad,” murmured the prince; and a ray of recollection seemed to flash across his face.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “My friend,” he continued, addressing Mosgliakoff, “I believe I forgot to tell you, there was a ballad sung—a ballad all about castles and knights; and some trou—badour or other came in. Of course, of course, I remember it all quite well. I recoll—ect I did turn over the ballad. It puzzles me much, for now it seems as though I had really heard the ballad, and not dreamt it all.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I confess, uncle,” said Mosgliakoff, as calmly as he could, though his voice shook with agitation, “I confess I do not see any difficulty in bringing your actual experience and your dream into strict conformity; it is consistent enough. You probably did hear the ballad. Miss Zenaida sings beautifully; probably you all adjourned into this room and Zenaida Afanassievna sang you the song. Of course, I was not there myself, but in all probability this ballad reminded you of old times; very likely it reminded you of that very vicomtesse with whom you used once to sing, and of whom you were speaking to-day; well, and then, when you went up for your nap and lay down, thinking of the delightful impressions made upon you by the ballad and all, you dreamed that you were in love and made an offer of marriage to the lady who had inspired you with that feeling.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna was struck dumb by this display of barefaced audacity.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Why, ye—yes, my boy, yes, of course; that’s exactly how it really wa—as!” cried the prince, in an ecstasy of delight.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Of course it was the de—lightful impressions that caused me to dream it. I certainly re—member the song; and then I went away and dreamed about my pro—posal, and that I really wished to marry! The viscountess was there too. How beautifully you have unravelled the diffi—culty, my dear boy. Well, now I am quite convinced that it was all a dream. Maria Alex—androvna! I assure you, you are under a delu—usion: it was a dream. I should not think of trifling with your feelings otherwise.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, indeed! Now I perceive very clearly whom we have to thank for making this dirty mess of our affairs!” cried Maria Alexandrovna, beside herself with rage, and turning to Mosgliakoff: “You are the man, sir—the dishonest person. It is you who stirred up this mud! It is you that puzzled an unhappy old idiot into this eccentric behaviour, because you yourself were rejected! But we shall be quits, my friend, for this offence! You shall pay, you shall pay! Wait a bit, my dishonest friend; wait a bit!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Maria Alexandrovna!” cried Mosgliakoff, blushing in his turn until he looked as red as a boiled lobster, “your words are so, so——to such an extent—I really don’t know how to express my opinion of you. No lady would ever permit herself to—to—. At all events I am but protecting my relative. You must allow that to allure an old man like this is, is——.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Quite so, quite so; allure,” began the prince, trying to hide himself behind Mosgliakoff.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Afanassy Matveyevitch!” cried Maria Alexandrovna, in unnatural tones; “do you hear, sir, how these people are shaming and insulting me? Have you quite exempted yourself from all the responsibilities of a man? Or are you actually a—a wooden block, instead of the father of a family? What do you stand blinking there for? eh! Any other husband would have wiped out such an insult to his family with the blood of the offender long ago.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Wife!” began Afanassy, solemnly, delighted, and proud to find that a need for him had sprung up for once in his life.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Wife, are you quite certain, now, that you did not dream all this? You might so easily have fallen asleep and dreamed it, and then muddled it all up with what really happened, you know, and so——”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: But Afanassy Matveyevitch was never destined to complete his ingenious, but unlucky guess.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Up to this moment the guests had all restrained themselves, and had managed, cleverly enough, to keep up an appearance of solid and judicial interest in the proceedings.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: But at the first sound, almost, of Afanassy’s voice, a burst of uncontrollable laughter rose like a tempest from all parts of the room.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna, forgetting all the laws of propriety in her fury, tried to rush at her unlucky consort; but she was held back by force, or, doubtless, she would have scratched out that gentleman’s eyes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Natalia Dimitrievna took advantage of the occasion to add a little, if only a little, drop more of poison to the bitter cup.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But, dear Maria Alexandrovna,” she said, in the sweetest honied tones, “perhaps it may be that it really was so, as your husband suggests, and that you are actually under a strange delusion?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “How! What was a delusion?” cried Maria Alexandrovna, not quite catching the remark.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Why, my dear Maria, I was saying, mightn’t it have been so, dear, after all? These sort of things do happen sometimes, you know!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What sort of things do happen, eh? What are you trying to do with me? What am I to make of you?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Why, perhaps, dear, you really did dream it all!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What? dream it! I dreamed it? And you dare suggest such a thing to me—straight to my face?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, why not? Perhaps it really was the case,” observed Felisata Michaelovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ye—yes, quite so, very likely it act—ually was the case,” muttered the old prince.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “He, too—gracious Heaven!” cried poor Maria Alexandrovna, wringing her hands.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Dear me, how you do worry yourself, Maria Alexandrovna. You should remember that dreams are sent us by a good Providence. If Providence so wills it, there is no more to be said. Providence gives the word, and we can neither weep nor be angry at its dictum.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Quite so, quite so. We can’t be a—angry about it,” observed the prince.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Look here; do you take me for a lunatic, or not?” said Maria Alexandrovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She spoke with difficulty, so dreadfully was she panting with fury.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: It was more than flesh and blood could stand.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She hurriedly grasped a chair, and fell fainting into it.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: There was a scene of great excitement.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “She has fainted in obedience to the laws of propriety!” observed Natalia Dimitrievna to Mrs. Antipova.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: But at this moment—at this moment when the general bewilderment and confusion had reached its height, and when the scene was strained to the last possible point of excitement, another actor suddenly stepped to the front; one who had been silent hitherto, but who immediately threw quite a different complexion on the scene.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Zenaida, or Zina Afanassievna, was an individual of an extremely romantic turn of mind.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I don’t know whether it really was that she had read too much of “that fool Shakespeare,” with her “little tutor fellow,” as Maria Alexandrovna insisted; but, at all events she was very romantic.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: However, never, in all her experience of Mordasoff life, had Zina before made such an ultra-romantic, or perhaps I might call it heroic, display as on the occasion of the sally which I am now about to describe.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Pale, and with resolution in her eyes, yet almost trembling with agitation, and wonderfully beautiful in her anger and scorn, she stepped to the front.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Gazing around at all, defiantly, she approached her mother in the midst of the sudden silence which had fallen on all present.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Her mother roused herself from her swoon at the first indication of a projected movement on Zina’s part, and she now opened her eyes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Mamma!” cried Zina, “why should we deceive anyone? Why befoul ourselves with more lies? Everything is so foul already that surely it is not worth while to bemean ourselves any further by attempting to gloss over the filth!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Zina, Zina! what are you thinking of? Do recollect yourself!” cried Maria Alexandrovna, frightened out of her wits, and jumping briskly up from her chair.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I told you, mamma—I told you before, that I should not be able to last out the length of this shameful and ignominious business!” continued Zina.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Surely we need no further bemean and befoul ourselves! I will take it all on myself, mamma. I am the basest of all, for lending myself, of my own free will, to this abominable intrigue! You are my mother; you love me, I know, and you wished to arrange matters for my happiness, as you thought best, and according to your lights. Your conduct, therefore, is pardonable; but mine! oh, no! never, never!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Zina, Zina! surely you are not going to tell the whole story? Oh! woe, woe! I felt that the knife would pierce my heart!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, mamma, I shall tell all; I am disgraced, you—we all of us are disgraced——”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Zina, you are exaggerating! you are beside yourself; and you don’t know what you are saying. And why say anything about it? The ignominy and disgrace is not on our side, dear child; I will show in a moment that it is not on our side!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “No, mamma, no!” cried Zina, with a quiver of rage in her voice, “I do not wish to remain silent any longer before these—persons, whose opinion I despise, and who have come here for the purpose of laughing at us. I do not wish to stand insult from any one of them; none of them have any right to throw dirt at me; every single one of them would be ready at any moment to do things thirty times as bad as anything either I or you have done or would do! Dare they, can they constitute themselves our judges?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Listen to that!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “There’s a pretty little speech for you!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Why, that’s us she’s abusing”!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “A nice sort of creature she is herself!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: These and other such-like exclamations greeted the conclusion of Zina’s speech.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, she simply doesn’t know what she’s talking about!” observed Natalia Dimitrievna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: We will make a digression, and remark that Natalia Dimitrievna was quite right there!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: For if Zina did not consider these women competent to judge herself, why should she trouble herself to make those exposures and admissions which she proposed to reveal in their presence?

Yes, Zina, so I did, while we read Shakespeare; and in theory I was pure and generous. Yet, how did I prove these qualities in practice?”

I am unworthy of your love, Zina! And you were good and true, not only in theory, but in practice too! You told your mother you would marry me, and no one else, and you would have kept your word! Do you know, Zina, I never realized before what you would sacrifice in marrying me! I could not even see that you might die of hunger if you did so! All I thought of was that you would be the bride of a great poet (in the future), and I could not understand your reasons for wishing to delay our union! So I reproached you and bullied you, and despised you and suspected you, and at last I committed the crime of showing your letter! I was not even a scoundrel at that moment! I was simply a worm-man. Ah! how you must have despised me! No, it is well that I am dying; it is well that you did not marry me! I should not have understood your sacrifice, and I should have worried you, and perhaps, in time, have learned to hate you, and ... but now it is good, it is best so! my bitter tears can at least cleanse my heart before I die. Ah! Zina! Zina! love me, love me as you did before for a little, little while! just for the last hour of my life. I know I am not worthy of it, but—oh, my angel, my Zina!”

text: Throughout this speech Zina, sobbing herself, had several times tried to stop the speaker; but he would not listen.

text: He felt that he must unburden his soul by speaking out, and continued to talk—though with difficulty, panting, and with choking and husky utterance.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, if only you had never seen me and never loved me,” said Zina, “you would have lived on now! Ah, why did we ever meet?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “No, no, darling, don’t blame yourself because I am dying! think of all my self-love, my romanticism! I am to blame for all, myself! Did they ever tell you my story in full? Do you remember, three years ago, there was a criminal here sentenced to death? This man heard that a criminal was never executed whilst ill! so he got hold of some wine, mixed tobacco in it, and drank it. The effect was to make him so dreadfully sick, with blood-spitting, that his lungs became affected; he was taken to a hospital, and a few weeks after he died of virulent consumption! Well, on that day, you know, after the letter, it struck me that I would do the same; and why do you think I chose consumption? Because I was afraid of any more sudden death? Perhaps. But, oh, Zina! believe me, a romantic nonsense played a great part in it; at all events, I had an idea that it would be striking and grand for me to be lying here, dying of consumption, and you standing and wringing your hands for woe that love should have brought me to this! You should come, I thought, and beg my pardon on your knees, and I should forgive you and die in your arms!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, don’t! don’t!” said Zina, “don’t talk of it now, dear! you are not really like that. Think of our happy days together, think of something else—not that, not that!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, but it’s so bitter to me, darling; and that’s why I must speak of it. I havn’t seen you for a year and a half, you know, and all that time I have been alone; and I don’t think there was one single minute of all that time when I have not thought of you, my angel, Zina! And, oh! how I longed to do something to earn a better opinion from you! Up to these very last days I have never believed that I should really die; it has not killed me all at once, you know. I have long walked about with my lungs affected. For instance, I have longed to become a great poet suddenly, to publish a poem such as has never appeared before on this earth; I intended to pour my whole soul and being into it, so that wherever I was, or wherever you were, I should always be with you and remind you of myself in my poems! And my greatest longing of all was that you should think it all over and say to yourself at last some day, ’No, he is not such a wretch as I thought, after all! It was stupid of me, Zina, stupid—stupid—wasn’t it, darling?”
